items.title: Correct Conduct Completes Celibacy, and Truthfulness Completes the Wholesome Verbal Side

items.zh: 不以愛染身觸母邑故，名遠離生臭。不行兩兩交會鄙事故，名遠離婬欲。不以餘手觸等方便而出不淨故，名非鄙愛，願受持梵行故，名遠離猥法。如是名為正行清淨具足。
items.en: Not touching another with bodily craving is called being free of foulness. Not engaging in the union of two bodies is called being free of sexual desire. Not bringing about a similarly impure release through the hand or other means is called being free of a lesser form of the same craving. Aspiring to genuinely uphold the celibate life is called being free of degraded conduct. This, taken together, constitutes the full completion of purity of correct conduct.
It should be understood that the summary meaning lies in this.

items.zh: 又翻妄語中，可信者，謂可委故。可委者，謂可寄託故。應可建立者，謂於彼彼違諍事中，應可建立為正證故。無有虛誑者，於委寄中不虛誑故，不欺誷故。
items.en: Reversing false speech: trustworthy means fit to be relied upon. Fit to be relied upon means fit to be entrusted with something. Fit to be established means fit to be called upon as an honest witness in any actual dispute. Free of deceit means never misleading or defrauding whatever has been entrusted.

items.zh: 此中略義者，謂顯三種攝受。一、欲解攝受，二、保任攝受，三、作用攝受。復次，法相差別建立者，謂即殺生、離殺生等。
items.en: The summary meaning here is that it shows three kinds of acceptance: first, acceptance through resolve; second, acceptance through undertaking; third, acceptance through action. Further, the establishment of the differences among the characteristics of dharmas means killing, abstaining from killing, and so on.

items.title: A New Lens Opens: The Ten Courses of Action by Their Own Formal Nature

items.zh: 云何殺生？謂於他眾生起殺欲樂，起染污心，若即於彼起殺方便，及即於彼殺究竟中所有身業。云何不與取？謂於他攝物起盜欲樂，起染污心，若即於彼起盜方便，及即於彼盜究竟中所有身業。
items.en: What is killing? It is: towards another sentient being, giving rise to the desire to kill, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then, towards that very being, initiating the effort to kill, together with whatever bodily action completes that killing. What is taking what is not given? It is: towards another's possessions, giving rise to the desire to steal, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then, towards that very possession, initiating the effort to steal, together with whatever bodily action completes that theft.

items.zh: 云何欲邪行？謂於所不應行，非道、非處、非時起習近欲樂，起染污心，若即於彼起欲邪行方便，及於欲邪行究竟中所有身業。
items.en: What is sexual misconduct? It is: towards what should not be approached, or through improper means, place, or time, giving rise to the desire for intimacy, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then initiating the effort towards that misconduct, together with whatever bodily action completes it.

items.title: The Four Verbal Courses and Two of the Three Mental Courses, by Their Formal Nature

items.zh: 云何妄語？謂於他有情起覆想說欲樂，起染污心，若即於彼起偽證方便，及於偽證究竟中所有語業。云何離間語？謂於他有情起破壞欲樂，起染污心，若即於彼起破壞方便，及於破壞究竟中所有語業。
items.en: What is false speech? It is: towards another sentient being, giving rise to the desire to conceal one's actual perception and speak otherwise, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then initiating the effort towards false testimony, together with whatever verbal action, once understood by the listener, completes it. What is divisive speech? It is: towards another sentient being, giving rise to the desire to cause a rift, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then initiating the effort towards that rift, together with whatever verbal action, once it actually causes the intended estrangement, completes it.

items.zh: 云何麁惡語？謂於他有情起麁語欲樂，起染污心，若即於彼起麁語方便，及於麁語究竟中所有語業。云何綺語？謂起綺語欲樂，起染污心，若即於彼起不相應語方便，及於不相應語究竟中所有語業。
items.en: What is harsh speech? It is: towards another sentient being, giving rise to the desire to speak harshly, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then initiating the effort towards harsh speech, together with whatever verbal action — the very act of hurling the abuse — completes it. What is frivolous speech? It is: giving rise to the desire to speak frivolously, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then initiating the effort towards speech that serves no genuine purpose, together with whatever verbal action, the very act of uttering it, completes it.

items.zh: 云何貪欲？謂於他所有起己有欲樂，起染污心，若於他所有起己有欲樂決定方便，及於彼究竟中所有意業。云何瞋恚？謂於他起害欲樂，起染污心，若於他起害欲樂決定方便，及於彼究竟中所有意業。
items.en: What is covetousness? It is: towards another's possessions, giving rise to the desire to make them one's own, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then settling into a determined resolve to do so, together with whatever mental action completes it. What is ill will? It is: towards another, giving rise to the desire to cause harm, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then settling into a determined resolve to do so, together with whatever mental action completes it.

items.title: Wrong View's Formal Nature, the Ten Wholesome Deeds by the Same Template, and Classification Closes

items.zh: 云何邪見？謂起誹謗欲樂，起染污心，若於起誹謗欲樂決定方便，及於彼究竟中所有意業。云何離殺生？謂於殺生起過患欲解，起勝善心，若於彼起靜息方便，及於彼靜息究竟中所有身業。如離殺生，如是離不與取乃至離邪見，應知亦爾。
items.en: What is wrong view? It is: giving rise to the desire to deny what is true, giving rise to a defiled mind, and then settling into a determined resolve to deny it, together with whatever mental action completes it. What is abstaining from killing? It is: coming to genuinely understand killing's own faults, giving rise to a superior wholesome mind, and then initiating the effort to bring it to rest, together with whatever bodily action completes that cessation. Just as with abstaining from killing, so too, in the very same way, with abstaining from taking what is not given, all the way through abstaining from wrong view.

items.zh: 此中差別者，謂於不與取起過患欲解，乃至於邪見起過患欲解，起勝善心，若於彼起靜息方便，及於彼靜息究竟中所有意業。
items.en: The distinction here is this: resolving that taking what is not given is a fault, and so on through resolving that wrong view is a fault; giving rise to an excellent wholesome mind; and whatever mental karma there is in the means of stilling them and in the completion of that stilling.

items.zh: 如是十種略為三種，所謂身業、語業、意業。即此三種廣開十種應知。
items.en: These ten, in brief, reduce to three: bodily karma, verbal karma, and mental karma. And these same three, expanded, should be understood to comprise the full ten.

items.title: Twelve Causes Behind Every Deed, and a Cautionary Tale About Judging Too Quickly

items.zh: 業因云何？應知有十二種相。一、貪，二、瞋，三、癡，四、自，五、他，六、隨他轉，七、所愛味，八、怖畏，九、為損害，十、戲樂，十一、法想，十二、邪見。
items.en: What are the causes of karma? There are, it should be understood, twelve. First, craving; second, hatred; third, delusion; fourth, one's own initiative; fifth, another's instigation; sixth, simply following others' lead; seventh, attachment to what is enjoyed; eighth, fear; ninth, the wish to cause harm; tenth, mere amusement; eleventh, the belief that the act is justified; twelfth, wrong view.

items.title: Five Stages of Karma, and Fascicle Eight Reaches Its Close

items.zh: 業位云何？應知略說有五種相。謂耎位，中位、上位、生位、習氣位。由耎不善業故，生傍生中。由中不善業故，生餓鬼中。由上不善業故，生那落迦中。由耎善業故，生人中。由中善業故，生欲界天中。由上善業故，生色、無色界。
items.en: What are the stages of karma? There are, briefly, five: the mild stage, the middling stage, the intense stage, the arising stage, and the habitual-trace stage. Through mild unwholesome karma, one is reborn among animals. Through middling unwholesome karma, one is reborn among hungry ghosts. Through intense unwholesome karma, one is reborn in the hells. Through mild wholesome karma, one is reborn as a human. Through middling wholesome karma, one is reborn in a desire-realm heaven. Through intense wholesome karma, one is reborn in the form or formless realm.

items.zh: 何等名為耎位不善業耶？謂以耎品貪瞋癡為因緣故。何等名為中位不善業耶？謂以中品貪瞋癡為因緣故。何等名為上位不善業耶？謂以上品貪瞋癡為因緣故。若諸善業，隨其所應，以無貪、無瞋、無癡為因緣應知。
items.en: What is called unwholesome karma at the mild stage? It is that which has mild greed, anger, and delusion as its conditions. What is called unwholesome karma at the middling stage? It is that which has middling greed, anger, and delusion as its conditions. What is called unwholesome karma at the intense stage? It is that which has intense greed, anger, and delusion as its conditions. Wholesome karma, as appropriate, should be understood as having non-greed, non-anger, and non-delusion as its conditions.

items.zh: 何等生位業？謂已生未滅現在前業。何等習氣位業？謂已生已滅不現前業。
items.en: What is karma in its arising stage? It is karma already arisen and not yet ceased, currently manifest before the mind. What is karma in its habitual-trace stage? It is karma already arisen and already ceased, no longer manifest at all.

blocks.text: The last reading of fascicle 8 completes the wholesome courses and then gives the second lens on karma: the **formal nature** of each deed, defined by a set of factors that every Buddhist ethics class uses to this day. It ends with the causes and grades of karma. This is practical moral psychology: it tells us exactly when an act becomes a full course of action.
The wholesome side completes celibacy (for those who keep it) and truthfulness. Each wholesome course is simply abstaining from the corresponding unwholesome one, with the intention to abstain.

subs.head: The formal nature of each deed

blocks.text: Each course of action is now defined by the same template:

items: the **object** (事): a living being, another's property, and so on;
the **perception** (想): perceiving it correctly as such;
the **affliction** (煩惱): greed, hatred, or delusion driving it;
the **completion** (究竟): the moment the deed is finished.

blocks.text: Killing, for example, is complete when the being dies, by one's means, with the intention and perception of killing it. Venerable Miào Jìng: theft is complete when the thing is lifted from its place (Day 56).

The verbal courses differ in when they are complete. Master Cháng Bǎi: false and divisive speech require the listener to take the words in, but harsh speech "is complete once the harsh words are hurled, whether or not the target understands". The three mental courses are complete in the mind alone: wrong view, for instance, once the resolve to deny is settled.

This template explains why the same outer act can be heavy or light karma: change the perception (one did not know), the intention (it was an accident), or the affliction (no hatred), and the act is no longer a full course of action.

The treatise lists twelve causes of karma, among them greed, hatred, delusion, habit, and the influence of others. Master Cháng Bǎi tells a cautionary story. On the metro, a young man in a priority seat was scolded by the whole carriage; only then did they see he was disabled. "The ancients taught: hold back three parts of what's on your tongue." We see the act, not its causes.

subs.head: Five stages, and grades of karma

blocks.text: Karma is graded mild, middling, and intense. Mild unwholesome karma leads to animal rebirth, middling to the ghost realm, intense to hell. Both teachers note that the *Avataṃsaka*'s chapter on the ten stages gives the opposite order for animals and ghosts; texts differ, and the principle, not the ranking, is what matters.

Both teachers tell of a nun who had the *Lotus Sūtra* copied. Lent to a monk, it appeared blank. Master Cháng Bǎi's explanation: the purity of one's mind varies, "sometimes a hundred, sometimes thirty", and the power of the deed varies with it. The same act, done with different minds, is different karma.

Fascicle 8 has given two complete manuals: one on the afflictions (their nature, causes, stages, and names) and one on karma (the ten courses, by person and by formal nature). The order is the treatise's teaching: affliction comes first, because affliction is what drives karma. Fascicle 9 completes the account of defilement with **rebirth defilement**: the twelve links of dependent origination.

quiz.q: The text defines each course by its formal nature, ending in completion. According to Master Cháng Bǎi, when is harsh speech complete?
options: once the abuse is uttered, regardless of understanding — unlike false or divisive speech, which require the listener to take it in
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Once the harsh words are hurled, harsh speech is complete in its formal nature, whether or not the target understands." False speech requires "the listeners to understand the testimony"; divisive speech, that "the targets take in the words." The translation's "the very act of hurling the abuse" matches.

quiz.q: The text lists twelve causes of karma. Master Cháng Bǎi tells of a priority seat on the metro. What does it illustrate?
options: a young man in a priority seat was scolded by everyone, until they saw he was disabled — "hold back three parts of what's on your tongue"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The whole car looked — the young man was lame; he was disabled"; "the ancients taught: hold back three parts of what's on your tongue, leaving room to reconsider." Among the twelve causes, "believing it justified" and "following others" can both produce karma.

quiz.q: The text says mild unwholesome karma leads to animals, middling to ghosts, intense to hell. Which scripture do the teachers note orders it differently?
options: the Avataṃsaka's Ten Grounds chapter — mild to ghosts, middling to animals, the reverse
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The *Avataṃsaka* says mild unwholesome karma leads to ghosts and middling to animals — exactly reversed." Venerable Miào Jìng: "The Ten Grounds chapter says ghosts are mild, animals middling; here it's the other way round." Master Cháng Bǎi's example of mild karma: pet dogs with grooming and doghouses.

quiz.q: Discussing mild, middling, and intense karma, both teachers tell of a nun who had the Lotus Sūtra copied. What does it illustrate?
options: the purity of reverence varies, and so does the deed's power — when lent to a monk, the copy appeared blank, for one's pure mind may be 100 one time and 30 another
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "When the monk took his seat and opened her copy, it was entirely blank — no words to be seen"; "one's pure mind is sometimes strong — perhaps 100, even 120 — sometimes only 30." Venerable Miào Jìng: she copied it breathing through a tube so her breath wouldn't touch the page. Wholesome karma too has grades, set by the degree of non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion.

quiz.q: According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what are the three stages of volition in making karma?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "In making karma, volition first deliberates, then decides, and finally impels." And: "Intention-karma is mental, comprising deliberation and decision; post-intention karma is bodily and verbal — impulsion." Venerable Miào Jìng: karma becomes grave with resolve — "determined to get it."

quiz.q: The text says knowing false speech means concealing one's perception, intention, or view. Venerable Miào Jìng tells of Maudgalyāyana predicting rain in seven days that didn't come. How did the Buddha judge it?
options: Maudgalyāyana said what he truly thought, so the Buddha ruled it was not false speech
the Buddha called it a grave lie
the Buddha said it rained later
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'With what mind did you say it?' 'With a true mind — I said what I thought.' The Buddha said this was not false speech." The key is concealing one's actual perception, intention, or view; being wrong isn't lying.
